original_question: Fix a Hilbert function H that occurs for a codimension-two complete intersection algebra. Can one determine all pairs of Jordan types (P, Q) that arise from multiplication by two linear forms ell_1 and ell_2 on an algebra A with H(A) = H?
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's actual target: it fixes a Hilbert function H coming from a codimension-two complete intersection, asks for a classification problem rather than existence of a single example, and asks for simultaneous Jordan data coming from two linear forms on the same algebra A.
missing_details: The algebra A should be stated explicitly to be a standard graded Artinian complete intersection of codimension (height) two, not just an arbitrary algebra with Hilbert function H.
The ambient ring should be made explicit: in the cited codimension-two classification [10], A is of the form A = k[x,y]/I.

The field assumptions behind the cited classification should be recorded: [10] works over an algebraically closed field k, with characteristic 0 or larger than the socle degree j for the Jordan-type classification.
The admissible Hilbert functions H should be identified as the codimension-two complete-intersection Hilbert functions, equivalently sequences of the form H = (1,2,...,d-1,d^k,d-1,...,2,1).
The linear forms should be specified as elements ell_1, ell_2 in A_1; the problem concerns their multiplication operators on A.
Jordan type should be defined explicitly as the partition of dim_k A given by the Jordan block decomposition of the nilpotent map m_{ell_i}: A -> A, a |-> ell_i a.
The quantifier should say that P and Q must occur simultaneously for the same algebra A, i.e. there exist one A and two linear forms ell_1, ell_2 on that A with those Jordan types.
It is implicit, but worth clarifying, that the problem is about pairs (P,Q) attached to the labeled forms ell_1 and ell_2; your draft does not say whether the pair is ordered.
It is also implicit that ell_1 and ell_2 are arbitrary linear forms, not necessarily generic and not necessarily distinct.
refined_question: Fix a codimension-two complete-intersection Hilbert function H. In the height-two complete-intersection setting of [10]—that is, for standard graded Artinian algebras A = k[x,y]/I over an algebraically closed field k with char(k) = 0 or char(k) > j, where j is the socle degree, and H(A) = H—determine all pairs of partitions (P,Q) for which there exist linear forms ell_1, ell_2 in A_1 such that P and Q are the Jordan types of the nilpotent multiplication maps m_{ell_1}, m_{ell_2}: A -> A.
justification: The draft is aiming directly at Question 5.9, whose wording is essentially the same classification problem for two linear forms. Section 5 supplies the local notation: Jordan type P_{ell,M} is attached to multiplication by ell, and in the graded case the relevant linear forms lie in A_1. Question 5.9 then asks for simultaneous realizability of two Jordan types P and Q for (ell_1,A) and (ell_2,A) with fixed H(A)=H. To make that question stand alone, one must import from the cited paper [10] the actual codimension-two complete-intersection setting in which the single-linear-form Jordan types are classified: A = k[x,y]/I, standard graded Artinian, H of CI form (1.1), and the characteristic assumptions under which the classification is proved. Corollaries 2.16 and 2.18 and Theorem 2.21 of [10] show that the individual Jordan types are already classified for fixed H, so the sharp remaining problem is exactly the simultaneous two-form version asked in Question 5.9.
